views.name: nyc_311_requests_event_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  created_date,
  DATE(created_date) AS created_date_date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) AS created_year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM created_date) AS created_month,
  EXTRACT(DAY FROM created_date) AS created_day,
  EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM created_date) AS created_dow,
  closed_date,
  DATE(closed_date) AS closed_date_date,
  status,
  agency,
  agency_name,
  complaint_type,
  descriptor,
  location_type,
  incident_zip,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(incident_address),''), NULL) AS incident_address,
  street_name,
  city,
  borough,
  community_board,
  CAST(bbl AS INT64) AS bbl,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  location,
  open_data_channel_type,
  resolution_description,
  resolution_action_updated_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_311.311_service_requests`

semantic_filters.status: no filter (preserve all statuses); created_date is assumed populated for events

views.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of 311 service requests with canonical date parts and preserved identifiers. Use when analyzing time-series, joining to spatial data, or aggregating by borough/complaint type. | Use for: time-series counts of 311 requests by borough/complaint_type; spatial joins to map requests to boundaries; average time-to-close (closed_date - created_date) by agency or complaint_type; top complaint types by community board or ZIP

views.name: citibike_trips_daily_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(starttime) AS trip_date,
  SAFE_CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  usertype,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(tripduration,0)) AS total_trip_seconds,
  AVG(NULLIF(tripduration,0)) AS avg_trip_seconds,
  APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(bikeid) AS distinct_bikes
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
GROUP BY trip_date, start_station_id, start_station_name, usertype

semantic_filters.starttime: assumes starttime is populated; no date range filter applied

views.description: Daily aggregated Citibike trip measures by start station id and usertype. Useful for ridership trends, station-level demand, and joins to station metadata. Preserves start date and station id for joins. | Use for: daily demand per station and user type; identify peak days for a station; compute time series for forecasting or seasonality; join to citibike_stations to get capacity/location

views.name: citibike_stations_point
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  short_name,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  region_id,
  capacity,
  rental_methods AS rental_methods,
  num_bikes_available,
  num_bikes_disabled,
  num_docks_available,
  num_docks_disabled,
  is_installed,
  is_renting,
  is_returning,
  eightd_has_key_dispenser,
  eightd_has_available_keys,
  last_reported
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_stations`
grain: one row per citibike station (station_id) representing current snapshot

semantic_filters.last_reported: no filter (preserve snapshot row(s)); may represent latest only depending on source

views.description: Cleaned station-level metadata and latest availability snapshot. Use to join spatially or to enrich trip aggregations. Preserves station_id and last_reported for temporal joins. | Use for: map station locations and capacities; compute bike availability ratios; join to trip aggregates to compute utilization

views.name: nypd_collisions_person_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  timestamp,
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough,
  on_street_name,
  off_street_name,
  cross_street_name,
  SAFE_CAST(zip_code AS STRING) AS zip_code,
  COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured,0) AS persons_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed,0) AS persons_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_injured,0) AS pedestrians_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_killed,0) AS pedestrians_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_injured,0) AS cyclists_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_killed,0) AS cyclists_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_motorist_injured,0) AS motorists_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed,0) AS motorists_killed,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_mv_collisions.nypd_mv_collisions`

semantic_filters.timestamp: no filter applied; keep all collisions

views.description: Per-collision summary of injured/killed counts for different road user types plus total persons. Useful when rolling up injuries/fatalities by time, borough, or contributing factor. | Use for: aggregate injuries/fatalities by borough/date; spatial hotspot mapping of collisions; compare vulnerable road user counts over time

views.name: subway_stations_with_complex
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id,
  s.station_name,
  s.complex_id,
  c.complex_name,
  s.division,
  s.line,
  s.station_lat,
  s.station_lon,
  s.borough_name,
  s.daytime_routes,
  s.structure
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.stations` AS s
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_complexes` AS c
ON s.complex_id = c.complex_id
grain: one row per subway station (station_id) as in stations table

semantic_filters.complex_id: no filter (preserve rows without complex match)

views.description: Station-level rows joined to their station complex names. Use to enrich station metadata for display or aggregation by complex. | Use for: group ridership by complex_name; map station complexes with station coordinates; join to station entrances for accessibility analysis

views.name: subway_entrances_ada_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  division,
  line,
  station_name,
  entrance_lat,
  entrance_lon,
  entry,
  exit_only,
  ada_compliant,
  corner,
  ada_notes,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_name ORDER BY CASE WHEN ada_compliant THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, entrance_lat, entrance_lon) AS entrance_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_entrances`
grain: one row per station entrance with a rank per station_name

semantic_filters.ada_compliant: no filter; ranking favors ada_compliant entrances first

views.description: Entrances with an entrance-level rank per station to allow deterministic selection of a representative entrance (e.g., nearest to centroid or first reported). Exposes entrance_rank for downstream top-K or dedup operations. | Use for: select a representative entrance per station (WHERE entrance_rank=1); analyze ADA coverage across representative entrances; map primary entrance locations for stations

views.name: taxi_trips_fare_breakdown
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  DATE(pickup_datetime) AS pickup_date,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) AS pickup_hour,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  rate_code,
  payment_type,
  fare_amount,
  extra,
  mta_tax,
  tip_amount,
  tolls_amount,
  imp_surcharge,
  total_amount,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  data_file_year,
  data_file_month
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_2023`
grain: one row per taxi trip record

semantic_filters.data_file_year: no specific year filter; preserves all rows in the table

views.description: Normalized projection of taxi trip fare components with date parts and preserved pickup/dropoff zone ids. Useful for revenue aggregation and temporal analysis. | Use for: aggregate revenue by zone/date/hour; compute average tip rates by payment_type; analyze demand by pickup_location_id
